title: THE STRENGTH OF A HUMBLE HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: (Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth.) — Num 12:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right in the middle of the story, Scripture pauses to tell us something about Moses: he was the most humble man on earth. It is a striking note, placed exactly when Moses is being attacked. While his own brother and sister tear him down, Moses does not fight back, does not defend himself, does not lash out.

That is what true humility looks like. It is not weakness or having a poor opinion of yourself. Humility is a quiet strength that does not need to prove itself or win every argument. Moses could afford to stay silent because he was not clinging to his position — he had entrusted it to God.

Notice who defends Moses in this chapter: God does. Moses does not have to lift a finger. When we are wronged, our instinct is to grab the microphone and set the record straight. But the humble person can leave their reputation in God's hands, trusting that He sees clearly and will act justly.

This points us straight to Jesus, who was "gentle and humble in heart," and who, when insulted, did not retaliate but entrusted Himself to the Father who judges justly. The path of humility is the path Christ walked, and it is the path He calls us to. You do not have to defend yourself when God is your defender.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you are criticised unfairly, do you defend yourself or entrust it to God?
2. What is the difference between humility and simply thinking little of yourself?
3. How does Jesus' example of humility challenge you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You were gentle and humble in heart even when insulted. Grow that same humility in me. Help me to trust God as my defender instead of fighting for myself. Amen.
